newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes drop sharply on December expiry sales.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes drop sharply on December expiry sales.

text.p: U.S. crudes closed dramatically lower in accordance with the tumultuous declines for the December contract on the NYMEX, which expired Wednesday.

Cash traders said the market was busy and in flux on the paper expiration, deflating Louisiana sweets and sour grades. Arbitrage for trans-Atlantic barrels widened as well, and wet Brent improved to trade 15 cts higher than the previous deals.
Outright crudes drifted all session, finally breaking down when the technical wall holding NYMEX spot futures near the $24.00 a barrel level severed.
December West Texas Intermediate/Cushing closed at $23.70-80 a barrel, 70 cts lower than the Tuesday settlement.
Cash dealers said there was plenty of "head scratching" after Wednesday's rough ride, as the exact reason for the assault on grade differentials escaped most players.
"There was a lot getting traded and plenty of craziness because of the December expiration," said one trader.
Late deals in the Light Lousiana Sweet/St. James were confirmed at a 90 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing, after trading earlier in the session at divergent levels.
LLS started off by selling at a $1.05-$1.10 premium, but dipped some 20 cts to deal at only an 80 cts edge. Other trades were seen at 85 cts and 87 cts over the WTI.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire declined 40 cts on the day.
Traders said HLS was last done at a 49 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing from plus 85-88 cts on Tuesday.
Midland/WTI was stable compared to the rest of the market, getting done late in the session at a steady 5 cts premium to the WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at a $1.80-$1.72 discount to the WTI marker, still within the weaker ranges established last week.
Eugene Island attracted deals as low as a $1.40 discount, after trading earlier at minus $1.16 and $1.25 to the WTI.
December Postings Plus talked late $1.80-$1.86, trading at $1.83, 12 cts weaker than the Tuesday range.
